# One sample lexeme per perly.y terminal the referee sentences use (spec section 8), joined by spaces to render a sentence.
# A third column is a preamble: source that must precede any sentence holding the terminal for the lexer to read its
# lexeme as that terminal (isa is a word until the feature is on; a PLUGIN_* word is a library operator only where
# testdata/libops's My::Ops declares it). A sentence's preambles are written once each, before its words, and their own
# tokens are not compared.
# GRAMPROG is a start selector, not a token, and renders to nothing. A terminal absent here has no single-lexeme
# rendering; every sentence holding one is on nonroundtrip-reviewed.txt. Those at 94e50866:
#   POSTJOIN    exists only inside an interpolated string, where the lexer makes one token
#   PERLY_DOLLAR  merges with the word after it into one variable token
QWLIST	qw(a)
PERLY_SEMICOLON	;
CHRELOP	<
CHEQOP	==
NCEQOP	<=>
SHIFTOP	>>
POWOP	**
MULOP	*
PERLY_QUESTION_MARK	?
PERLY_COLON	:
OROR	||
MATCHOP	=~
DOTDOT	..
DORDOR	//
BITOROP	|
BITANDOP	&
ASSIGNOP	=
ANDAND	&&
ADDOP	+
REFGEN	\
NOTOP	not
POSTINC	++
POSTDEC	--
METHCALL0	meth
ARROW	->
PERLY_COMMA	,
UNIOP	ref
PREINC	++
PREDEC	--
PERLY_TILDE	~
PERLY_PLUS	+
PERLY_MINUS	-
PERLY_EXCLAMATION_MARK	!
LOOPEX	last
KW_REQUIRE	require
KW_MY	my
KW_LOCAL	local
KW_DO	do
OROP	or
ANDOP	and
LSTOP	print
BAREWORD	foo
PERLY_BRACKET_OPEN	[
PERLY_BRACKET_CLOSE	]
PERLY_BRACE_OPEN	{
PERLY_BRACE_CLOSE	}
UNIOPSUB	foo
BLKLSTOP	any
NCRELOP	isa	use feature "isa";
PLUGIN_LOW_OP	lowop	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_LOGICAL_OR_LOW_OP	orlow	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_LOGICAL_AND_LOW_OP	andlow	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_ASSIGN_OP	assign	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_LOGICAL_OR_OP	oror	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_LOGICAL_AND_OP	andand	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_REL_OP	same	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_ADD_OP	plus	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_MUL_OP	mul	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_POW_OP	pow	use My::Ops;
PLUGIN_HIGH_OP	high	use My::Ops;
